01 / THE CHALLENGE

The challenge

Medical education, clinical decision support and hospital documentation presented different needs and adoption barriers. The task was to find where a product could deliver measurable value and fit institutional workflows.

02 / THE APPROACH

The approach

Conducted 370+ structured interviews over 18 months across students, clinicians and hospital administrators. Built Kaya with adaptive case progression, real-time diagnostic feedback and clinical-performance analytics, incorporating learner feedback across four iteration cycles.

03 / WHAT CHANGED

What changed

Field evidence led to two strategic pivots: from medical-education simulation to clinical decision support, then to hospital documentation automation. Conversations with 10 hospital systems highlighted documentation burden as a priority. These are discovery and product-development outcomes, rather than evidence of sustained adoption.

IN THE DETAILS

What the interviews revealed

Three recurring barriers were EHR integration complexity, documentation overhead and uncertainty around reimbursement and data governance. Kano analysis, PESTEL evaluation and financial viability assessments helped compare the opportunities.

IN THE DETAILS

Two decisions to change direction

In 2024–2025, institutional research shifted attention from simulation to diagnostic support. In 2025, conversations with 10 hospital systems redirected the work toward documentation automation. The product direction followed the workflow problem and willingness to adopt.

IN THE DETAILS

Research beyond the interviews

Compared 12 clinical AI vendors across positioning, features, pricing and go-to-market strategies. Created five institutional workflow demonstrations and partner-engagement materials informed by research and pilot learnings. Several discussions advanced to pilot proposals; proposals are distinct from commercial deployments.

THE TAKEAWAY

Changing direction is useful when it is grounded in evidence. Discovery earns its place when it changes what gets built.
